args.body:
HARROW & VANE LLP — COUNTER-REDLINE COVER NOTE

To: Dahlgren & Pike LLP (counsel to Corvid Analytics LLC)
From: Harrow & Vane LLP (counsel to Northgale Systems, Inc.)
Date: [2026]
Re: Northgale Systems, Inc. / Corvid Analytics LLC — Master Services Agreement — Northgale counter-turn redline to Corvid rev B counter-draft

This cover note accompanies Northgale Systems, Inc.'s (Customer) counter-turn redline to Corvid Analytics LLC's (Provider) rev B counter-draft of the Northgale client-form Master Services Agreement. Each response below is grounded in Northgale's 2026 Commercial Contracting Playbook (internal — Legal Department) and responds to every tracked change in Corvid's rev B transmitted 9 July 2026. All other terms of the client form v2 (execution-ready base) are accepted as drafted.

For each rev B change, Northgale states whether it accepts, counters at an approved playbook fallback, or rejects:

1. Section 2.2 — Renewal period. Corvid rev B changes the renewal period from one (1) year to successive two (2) year renewal periods.
Response: REJECT. Under playbook PB-1 there is no approved fallback for multi-year renewal periods of any length; any multi-year renewal period is out of policy and requires Chief Legal Officer approval, which is not being granted at this time. Northgale counters and will hold the standard of automatic renewal in successive one (1) year renewal periods. Counter figure: one (1) year renewal periods.

2. Section 4.3 — Late interest rate. Corvid rev B increases interest on late undisputed amounts from 1.0% per month to 1.5% per month.
Response: REJECT. Under playbook PB-4, late interest is never to exceed 1.0% per month. Corvid's 1.5% exceeds the policy ceiling. Northgale counters and will hold the playbook ceiling. Counter figure: late interest at 1.0% per month (or the maximum lawful rate, whichever is lower), as in the client form.

3. New Section 4.4 — Suspension of Services. Corvid rev B adds a right for Provider to suspend Services if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid fifteen (15) days after its due date.
Response: COUNTER (at approved playbook position). Under playbook PB-4, suspension-of-services rights are out of policy unless preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice, and any suspension right of any kind requires the CFO's sign-off, which has not been provided. Northgale does not accept Corvid's 15-day suspension trigger. Northgale counters that any suspension right is contingent on (i) at least thirty (30) days' prior written cure notice to Customer before any suspension, and (ii) prior CFO authorization. Counter figure: suspension right, if any, requires at least 30 days' written cure notice and prior CFO sign-off (Corvid's 15-day trigger rejected).

4. Section 7.2 — Termination for convenience notice. Corvid rev B increases Customer's termination-for-convenience notice from thirty (30) days to ninety (90) days.
Response: COUNTER (at approved playbook fallback). Under playbook PB-2, the approved fallback ceiling is forty-five (45) days' notice; any notice period above 45 days requires CLO approval, which is not being granted. Northgale does not accept Corvid's 90-day period. Northgale counters at the approved fallback. Counter figure: forty-five (45) days' prior written notice.

5. New Section 7.4 — Wind-down. Corvid rev B adds a wind-down period of sixty (60) days upon any termination other than for Provider's uncured material breach, during which Customer pays the full monthly base service fee for wind-down services plus all committed third-party costs.
Response: COUNTER (at approved playbook position). Under playbook PB-3, a wind-down is acceptable only if (i) it is capped at thirty (30) days and (ii) compensation is limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments; full-fee wind-down compensation is out of policy. Northgale does not accept Corvid's 60-day term or its full-fee compensation basis. Northgale counters. Counter figures: wind-down duration capped at thirty (30) days; compensation basis limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments (not full monthly base service fee).

6. Section 9.1 — Liability-cap measurement period. Corvid rev B shortens the cap measurement period from the twenty-four (24) months preceding the first event giving rise to liability to twelve (12) months.
Response: COUNTER (at approved playbook fallback). Under playbook PB-5, the approved fallback floor for the measurement period is eighteen (18) months; a twelve (12) month period is below the floor and would require CLO approval, which is not being granted. Northgale does not accept Corvid's 12-month period. Northgale counters at the approved fallback floor. Counter figure: liability cap measured at the Fees paid or payable by Customer in the eighteen (18) months preceding the first event giving rise to liability.

7. Section 9.2 — Carve-outs. Corvid rev B deletes clause (c), which excludes gross negligence and willful misconduct from the liability cap.
Response: REJECT. Under playbook PB-5, the carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct are non-negotiable; deletion of any such carve-out requires joint CLO and CFO approval, which is not being granted. Northgale does not accept the deletion of clause (c). Northgale rejects the deletion and retains clause (c) as drafted in the client form. Counter treatment: clause (c) (a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct) remains outside the Section 9.1 cap.

8. Section 11.2 — Service-credit cap. Corvid rev B lowers the aggregate monthly service-credit cap from 20% of the monthly base service fee to 10%.
Response: COUNTER (at approved playbook fallback). Under playbook PB-6, the approved fallback floor for the aggregate monthly credit cap is fifteen percent (15%); a 10% cap is out of policy. Northgale does not accept Corvid's 10% cap. Northgale counters at the approved fallback floor. Counter figure: aggregate service-credit cap of 15% of the monthly base service fee in any calendar month.

For clarity: Corvid's earlier rev A markup has been superseded in full by rev B and is not addressed here, consistent with the 9 July 2026 transmittal to disregard it.

Out-of-policy items not accepted at the fallback (including the two-year renewal request and any term breaching a policy floor) are the subject of Northgale's separate escalation/approval memorandum for the Deal Committee. Questions should be directed to Meredith Okafor, General Counsel, Northgale Systems, Inc.

Harrow & Vane LLP
Counsel to Northgale Systems, Inc.
